answer: A bonded staking protocol suppresses Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock financial collateral in an escrow contract before joining the network. To repel a tide of synthetic replicas, an identity is registered through a walnut validation contract and bound to a falcon signing key. An attacker must commit scarce liquid capital per deployed persona, facing slashing if malicious behavior occurs. However, this mechanism favors well-funded entities, pricing out low-budget autonomous agents.
